material_systems.name: Interior Adhesion Primer
material_systems.description: Water-based adhesion promoter for previously painted interior doors. Bonds to glossy, chalky, or oil-based existing coatings without full mechanical sanding. Primary RP primer for sound-to-peeling conditions. Doors historically received oil-based paint (semi-gloss default sheen) making adhesion primer especially critical when solvent test confirms alkyd base.

products.notes: Water-based for low VOC and easy cleanup. Bonds to glossy surfaces without full mechanical sanding. For SS_INT_SOUND_PAINT: use only when adhesion test is marginal or existing sheen is semi-gloss+. For SS_INT_FAILING_PAINT: spot prime scraped areas, full prime if bare >30%. For SS_INT_PEELING: full surface prime after complete scrape. Doors are semi-gloss by default making adhesion primer more frequently required than on walls.

prime_scope_by_state.SS_INT_SOUND_PAINT: conditional -- skip if adhesion test passes on low-sheen surfaces; apply if marginal adhesion or high-sheen existing finish or oil-based base identified
prime_scope_by_state.SS_INT_FAILING_PAINT: spot prime scraped areas (<30% bare) or full prime (>=30% bare)
prime_scope_by_state.SS_INT_PEELING: full surface prime -- extensive bare area after complete scrape

material_systems.cleanup: Water cleanup. Standard latex cleanup procedure.

material_systems.name: Interior Stain-Blocking Primer (Shellac-Based)
material_systems.description: Shellac-based stain blocker for smoke-damaged doors. Full-surface application required -- smoke contamination is pervasive even when not visually apparent. Panel doors trap concentrated smoke/nicotine deposits in rail-stile joints and panel crevices. Latex and acrylic primers have ZERO stain blocking capability (RC-002).

products.notes: Shellac is the ONLY product that reliably seals nicotine/smoke residue. Full surface application required. Strong odor -- requires ventilation. Fast dry (~45 min recoat). NOT water-cleanup -- requires denatured alcohol for tool cleaning. Panel door crevices trap concentrated smoke deposits -- ensure full coverage of all profile details.

material_systems.cleanup: Denatured alcohol. Standard water cleanup does NOT work for shellac. CON_DENATURED_ALCOHOL required.

material_systems.name: Interior Mildew-Resistant Primer
material_systems.description: Mildew-resistant primer with antimicrobial additives for moisture-damaged doors. Applied after biocide treatment and full drying. Most common on bathroom door frame bottoms where moisture wicks into end grain. Gate condition: moisture SOURCE must be resolved before painting.

products.notes: Apply only after biocide treatment and full drying (24+ hrs). Contains antimicrobial additives preventing spore regrowth under paint film. Gate condition: active moisture source MUST be resolved by other trades. Bathroom/kitchen door frames are the most common application -- moisture enters at frame-to-floor joint and wicks into end grain.

prime_scope_by_state.SS_INT_MOISTURE_DAMAGE: full surface prime on all affected areas -- mildew spores may be present beyond visible damage area

material_systems.cleanup: Water cleanup. Standard latex cleanup procedure.

material_systems.name: Standard Acrylic Trim Enamel
material_systems.description: 100% acrylic enamel for standard residential door repaint at QT3. Fast dry/recoat, non-yellowing, water cleanup. Standard production grade. Same product selection as NC door and trim finish. Lower hardness than alkyd -- blocking risk on doors (hinge side contact). Adequate for production work but not ideal for high-traffic doors.

example_products: Sherwin-Williams ProClassic Waterborne Interior Acrylic Enamel
Benjamin Moore Regal Select Interior Semi-Gloss
products.notes: Fast dry/recoat. Non-yellowing. Water cleanup. Standard production grade. Same product as NC door finish at QT3. Lower hardness than alkyd -- monitor for blocking on hinge side.

material_systems.notes: Standard production system for QT3 door RP. Satin is the only sheen available at QT3. Material systems are recommendations -- contractor has discretion on product selection.

material_systems.name: Modified Urethane Trim Enamel
material_systems.description: Urethane-modified alkyd / waterbased alkyd for premium residential door repaint at QT4. Superior flow and leveling, harder cured film. SHORT working time -- apply, tip once, walk away per FFD 15.3.1. Do not overwork. Blocking resistant -- ideal for doors. Extended cure time (7+ days full hardness) -- door rehang timing critical.

example_products: Benjamin Moore Advance Waterborne Interior Alkyd
Sherwin-Williams Pro Industrial Waterbased Alkyd Urethane
products.notes: Superior flow and leveling. Harder cured film. SHORT working time -- apply, tip once, walk away (FFD 15.3.1). Do not overwork. Blocking resistant -- ideal for door slab contact surfaces. Extended cure time (7+ days full hardness) -- coordinate door rehang timing.

material_systems.notes: Premium residential standard for QT4 door RP. Semi-gloss is traditional/default door sheen at this tier. Material systems are recommendations -- contractor has discretion.

material_systems.name: Premium Urethane Trim Enamel
material_systems.description: Premium acrylic-urethane enamel for superior door repaint at QT5. Maximum durability, excellent leveling, hardest film. SHORT working time -- apply, tip once, walk away per FFD 15.3.1. Emerald Urethane is an acrylic-urethane enamel, NOT a waterborne alkyd (RC-006).

products.coat_notes: QT5 brush typically requires 3 coats per FFD 15.10.3. QT5 spray: 2 coats standard.
products.notes: Maximum durability. Excellent leveling. Hardest film. SHORT working time -- apply, tip once, walk away (FFD 15.3.1). Emerald Urethane is an acrylic-urethane enamel, NOT a waterborne alkyd (RC-006). Sands easily between coats.

material_systems.notes: Premium/custom home standard for QT5 door RP. Gloss available only at this tier. Material systems are recommendations -- contractor has discretion.

ITM_DOOR_FRAME_SET.notes: One frame set = ~30 SF equivalent (head jamb + 2 side jambs + door stop). Previously painted substrate absorbs less primer than bare wood. Higher coverage than NC bare-wood primer (300-350 SF/gal).

ITM_DOOR_SLAB_RP.notes: One door slab side = ~20 SF (3'0" x 6'8" standard = 20 SF face + edge). Previously painted surface absorbs less than bare wood.

coverage_profiles.notes: Adhesion primer on previously painted door surfaces. Lower porosity than bare wood results in higher coverage vs NC primer profiles (COV_FRAME_PRIMER_BARE at 300 SF/gal). Coverage is consistent across door types for primer -- complexity modifier does not affect primer coverage significantly because primer does not need to achieve profile fill.
assumptions: Previously painted substrate -- lower absorption than bare wood
Standard door: 3'0" x 6'8" (20 SF face), frame set ~30 SF
Door type complexity does not significantly affect primer coverage rate

ITM_DOOR_FRAME_SET.notes: Shellac stain blocker has lower coverage than latex adhesion primer due to higher solids content. Frame joints and stop crevices trap smoke residue requiring thorough coverage.

ITM_DOOR_SLAB_RP.notes: Panel door crevices (rail-stile joints, panel edges) require additional material. Flat/slab doors slightly higher coverage.

coverage_profiles.notes: Shellac-based stain blocker has lower coverage than latex primers due to higher solids content and heavier required film build. Full surface application required on smoke-damaged doors.
assumptions: Full surface application on smoke-damaged doors
Shellac products have higher solids, lower spread rate than latex
Panel door crevices require additional material

ITM_DOOR_FRAME_SET.notes: Mildew primer coverage similar to adhesion primer -- latex-based formula. Slightly lower than adhesion due to thicker recommended film build for antimicrobial effectiveness. Typically applied to frame only (slab rarely moisture-damaged).

ITM_DOOR_SLAB_RP.notes: Slab-side mildew priming is rare -- moisture damage typically concentrates at frame bottom. Included for completeness.

coverage_profiles.notes: Mildew-resistant primer coverage similar to adhesion primer (latex-based formula). Slightly thicker recommended film build for antimicrobial effectiveness. Typically applied to frame (moisture damage at frame bottom) rather than slab.
assumptions: Latex formula -- similar coverage to adhesion primer
Slightly thicker film build for antimicrobial effectiveness
Frame is primary target; slab mildew priming is uncommon

ITM_DOOR_FRAME_SET.notes: Finish coat on primed/prepared frame surface. Equivalent to NC frame finish coverage (COV_FRAME_FINISH at 400 SF/gal) because substrate condition after prime is equivalent.

slab.notes: Flat/flush door -- minimal surface area per side, no crevices. Slightly higher coverage.

panel.notes: Panel doors (4-panel, 6-panel, raised panel) -- rail-stile joints and panel recesses reduce coverage. Material settles in panel crevices.

french.notes: French doors -- multiple muntins increase surface area significantly. Material used on narrow muntin profiles. Does NOT include glass pane area.

bifold.notes: Bifold panels -- smaller than standard door, less material per side.

louvered.notes: Louvered doors -- many slat edges dramatically increase surface area. Spray-only for RP (brush impractical on louvers).

ITM_DOOR_SLAB_RP.notes: Finish coat on primed/prepared slab surface. Door type affects coverage rate significantly -- panel crevices and louvered slats increase material consumption. Standard rate (20 ea_side/gal) is weighted average across typical residential mix.

coverage_profiles.notes: Finish coat coverage on primed door surfaces. Frame coverage equivalent to NC (COV_FRAME_FINISH). Slab coverage varies significantly by door type -- louvered at 8 ea_side/gal vs bifold at 25 ea_side/gal. Coat count: QT3-QT4 = 2 coats, QT5 brush = 3 coats per FFD 15.10.3.
assumptions: Primed smooth surface -- equivalent to NC after prime
Two-coat system standard; third coat at QT5 brush has same per-coat coverage
Door type mix assumed 60% panel, 20% slab, 10% bifold, 5% French, 5% louvered for weighted average

consumables.name: RP Assessment Kit (adhesion test + coating ID)
consumables.specification: Cross-hatch cutter, pressure-sensitive tape (ASTM D3359), mineral spirits, white rags for coating identification solvent test
consumables.notes: RP-specific assessment supplies. One kit per project. Includes ASTM D3359 cross-hatch adhesion test materials and solvent test supplies for latex vs oil-based coating identification. Doors are HIGH RISK for oil-based existing paint -- coating ID is critical. Shared across interior RP specs.

consumables.name: TSP (Trisodium Phosphate) Cleaner
consumables.specification: Powdered or liquid TSP concentrate, mixed per manufacturer directions
consumables.notes: RP door-specific decontamination wash. Removes hand oils, cleaning chemical residue, grease, and surface contaminants from existing paint before coating. Doors accumulate more hand/body oil than any other interior surface. One quart of concentrate makes enough solution for ~30 door openings (frame + slab). Not used in NC (new substrate is clean).

consumables.name: Liquid Sander / Deglosser
consumables.specification: Liquid sander/deglosser for chemical degloss of existing paint, Krud Kutter Gloss-Off or equivalent
consumables.notes: RP-specific: chemical degloss for existing semi-gloss/gloss door paint. Dulls existing sheen to promote adhesion without full mechanical sanding. One quart covers ~15 door openings (frame + both slab sides). Especially useful on panel doors where mechanical sanding cannot reach all rail-stile joint crevices. Not used in NC. Shared across interior RP specs.

consumables.name: Wood Hardener / Consolidant
consumables.specification: Penetrating wood consolidant, Minwax Wood Hardener or equivalent
consumables.notes: For moisture-damaged frame bottoms where wood substrate is softened. Penetrating consolidant stabilizes wood fibers before filling/priming. One pint treats ~8 frame bottom sections (worst case). Conditional on SS_INT_MOISTURE_DAMAGE + soft substrate finding during assessment. Not used in NC (no moisture-damaged substrate). Bathroom/kitchen door frames are primary use case.

consumables.name: Contour Sanding Sponge
consumables.specification: Flexible sanding sponge, medium/fine grit (150-220), angled edges for profile conformance
consumables.notes: Flexible sanding sponge for panel door prep and interstage. Conforms to rail-stile joints, raised panel bevels, and stop molding profiles where rigid blocks cannot reach. Essential for panel, raised panel, and French doors. Per Fine_Finish_Doctrine: flexible sponges for profile-following only, NOT for defect leveling (use rigid block for flat surfaces).

consumables.name: Sandpaper 120-grit
consumables.specification: Sandpaper sheet, 120 grit, 9x11 inch
consumables.notes: Aggressive grit for feathering scrape edges on failing/peeling doors. Creates smooth transition from scraped to sound paint. Non-negotiable at all tiers -- feathering must be thorough on doors (viewed at close range). One sheet covers ~4 door openings (frame + slab sides) for scrape edge feathering.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 150-grit
consumables.specification: Sandpaper sheet, 150 grit, 9x11 inch
consumables.notes: General prep grit for degloss scuff sanding and mechanical surface preparation on sound paint. All tiers. One sheet per ~5 door openings for mechanical degloss.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 220-grit
consumables.specification: Sandpaper sheet, 220 grit, 9x11 inch

grit_by_tier.QT3: 220 -- spot sand nibs and rough spots only
grit_by_tier.QT4: 220 -- full surface sand for adhesion and leveling

consumables.notes: Interstage sanding between finish coats. Spot sand at QT3, full surface at QT4. Also used for light sand of primer before finish. One sheet per ~4 door sides for interstage sanding. Rigid sanding block mandatory for flat surfaces per FFD 15.4.1.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 320-grit
consumables.specification: Sandpaper sheet, 320 grit, 9x11 inch
consumables.notes: QT5 interstage sanding between finish coats. Thorough 320-grit sanding per FFD 15.10.3. Uniform scratch pattern required. One sheet per ~3 door sides (more thorough sanding at QT5). Rigid sanding block mandatory per FFD 15.4.1.

consumables.name: Sanding block (fine grit range)
consumables.specification: Rigid sanding block, fine grit range (150-220)
consumables.notes: Rigid blocks remove defects -- mandatory per FFD 15.4.1 for between-coat sanding on flat door surfaces (slab field, frame jamb flats). Flexible sponges are NOT acceptable for defect leveling. Use CON_SANDING_SPONGE_CONTOUR for profiled areas only. One block per crew, reusable across coats.

consumables.name: Lightweight spackling compound
consumables.specification: Lightweight spackling compound, tub or squeeze tube
consumables.notes: For patching scrape edges, filling gouges, and repairing defects revealed after degloss/scrape on RP doors. GOOD condition typically has no fill work. FAIR/POOR condition: fill scraped transition areas, surface defects, and small dents. One quart per ~20 door openings at FAIR condition.

consumables.name: Paintable acrylic latex caulk
consumables.specification: Paintable acrylic latex caulk, white, 10.1 oz tube
consumables.notes: For caulk assess/replace at frame-to-casing joints on RP doors. RP caulk replacement is selective -- assess each joint, replace only deteriorated sections. ~10 door frames per tube because partial re-caulk (not full run). NC rate was 8-10 frames per tube for full caulk. Allow cure time before coating.

consumables.name: Caulk gun
consumables.specification: Standard caulk gun, ratchet-type
consumables.notes: Reusable tool for caulk application. One per crew.

consumables.name: Angled sash brush (2-2.5 inch)
consumables.specification: 2-2.5 inch angled sash brush, synthetic bristle (nylon/polyester blend)
consumables.notes: Primary brush application tool for door finish and primer. One per painter per material type (primer brush + finish brush). Also used for touch-up/detail with spray method. Quality brush essential for smooth finish on doors -- scrutinized surface. Per Materials_and_Consumables_Doctrine: 1 brush per material type.

consumables.name: Angled sash brush (1.5 inch) for detail
consumables.specification: 1.5 inch angled sash brush, synthetic bristle, for panel crevice and frame stop detail
consumables.notes: Smaller detail brush for panel door crevices (rail-stile joints, panel recess corners), frame stop surfaces, and frame inside corners. Optional supplement to primary 2-2.5 inch brush. One per material type when panel doors are in scope.

consumables.name: Brush for shellac (dedicated)
consumables.specification: 2-inch angled sash brush, dedicated for shellac use, natural or synthetic bristle
consumables.notes: Dedicated brush for shellac stain-blocking primer (BIN). Shellac requires alcohol cleanup -- keep separate from latex brushes. Conditional on smoke damage substrate state.

consumables.name: Airless spray tip 310-411 (fine finish)
consumables.specification: Airless spray tip, 310-411 range (6-8 inch fan, 0.010-0.011 orifice) for fine-finish door/trim
consumables.notes: Fine-finish spray tips for doors. Tight fan pattern for frame width and slab face. Fine atomization for smooth finish. One tip per ~20 doors (combined frame + slab). Replace when pattern degrades.

consumables.name: Spray gun filter
consumables.specification: In-line filter for airless spray gun
consumables.notes: Replace when clogged or every ~50 gallons. One per spray setup.

consumables.name: Tack cloth
consumables.specification: Resin-impregnated cheesecloth for dust removal
consumables.notes: Wipe door surfaces immediately before each coat application to remove sanding dust. Essential for quality finish per Fine_Finish_Doctrine Section 15.12. One tack cloth covers ~6 door openings (frame + slab sides). Use before every coat for dust-free surface.

consumables.name: Flexible putty knife
consumables.specification: Flexible putty knife, 1.5-inch or 2-inch
consumables.notes: For applying lightweight spackle to defects and scrape edges. Flexible blade for flush fill on door and frame surfaces. One per crew, reusable.

consumables.name: Blue painter's tape 1.5-inch
consumables.specification: Blue painter's tape, 1.5-inch width, 180 LF per roll (60 yards)
consumables.notes: For hardware masking (brush method: 3 hinges + lockset + strike plate per door), wall edge masking at frame-to-wall junction (spray method), and attaching masking paper. Per Materials_and_Consumables_Doctrine: 180 LF (60 yards) per roll regardless of width. Usage: brush ~6 LF per door opening for hardware, spray ~20 LF per door opening for wall masking.

consumables.name: Masking paper 12-inch
consumables.specification: Masking paper, 12-inch width, 180 LF per roll (60 yards)
consumables.notes: For wall masking adjacent to door opening during spray application. 12-inch width covers wall adjacent to frame head and sides. Attached with blue tape. Per Materials_and_Consumables_Doctrine: 180 LF (60 yards) per roll. Spray method only -- brush method uses tape line only.

consumables.name: Canvas drop cloth
consumables.specification: Canvas drop cloth, 4x12 ft runner or 4x5 ft compact
consumables.notes: Floor protection at door location for brush method drip containment. Runner-style or compact drop positioned under door opening. 1-2 per painter, reusable. RP always has finished floors -- floor protection is mandatory.

consumables.name: Rosin paper
consumables.specification: Rosin paper roll, 36-inch width, 500 SF per roll
consumables.notes: 8-foot radius floor protection for spray overspray containment around each door opening. Per PS_PROTECT_SF.FLOOR_8FT_RADIUS input. Taped at seams and edges with blue tape.

consumables.name: Plastic sheeting 4 mil
consumables.specification: 4 mil plastic sheeting for wall/furniture protection during spray
consumables.notes: Wall and furniture protection for spray application in occupied homes. Heavier weight (4 mil) prevents tear during work. Drape over furniture in door swing arc, cover wall surfaces adjacent to door opening beyond masking paper range.

consumables.name: Blue painter's tape 3/4-inch (glass masking)
consumables.specification: Blue painter's tape, 3/4-inch width, 180 LF per roll (60 yards)
consumables.notes: For glass pane masking on French doors. Narrow 3/4-inch tape follows muntin edges around each pane. ~5 LF per pane (perimeter of one pane). Driven by PS_META.EA.DOOR_PANES_TOTAL input. French door 15-lite = ~75 LF per side.

consumables.name: Denatured alcohol
consumables.specification: Denatured alcohol for shellac cleanup
consumables.notes: Required for cleaning brushes and tools used with shellac stain-blocking primer (BIN). Standard water cleanup does NOT work for shellac. One quart per project. Conditional on smoke damage substrate state.

consumables.name: Painter's pyramids
consumables.specification: Plastic painter's pyramids for elevating doors during painting
consumables.notes: Elevate removed door slabs during spray painting for full-surface access. 4 per door (standard configuration). Reusable across all doors. Per Materials_and_Consumables_Doctrine: include when doors in scope. Spray method removes doors from hinges for horizontal spray.

consumables.name: Zip-lock bags for hardware
consumables.specification: Gallon-size zip-lock bags for hardware storage and labeling
consumables.notes: For bagging and labeling removed hardware (hinges, locksets, strike plates). Spray method removes all hardware from doors. One bag per door opening. Label with door location for accurate reinstall. Essential for occupied-home spray work.

floor_perimeter.description: Localized floor protection at door location for brush method drip containment

floor_full_8ft_radius.description: Radial floor protection for spray overspray containment around door opening

wall_adjacent_door.description: Wall masking around door opening during spray application

hardware_covers.description: Hardware masking (brush method) or removal/bagging (spray method)
hardware_covers.notes: Brush: mask 3 hinges + lockset + strike plate with tape. Spray: remove all hardware, bag, label, reinstall after cure. Method-dependent protection strategy.

floor_door_swing.description: Door swing arc protection -- typically subsumed by spray floor protection
floor_door_swing.notes: Usually covered by floor_full_8ft_radius for spray. May be separate for brush touch-up work.

glass_mask.description: Glass pane masking for French doors
glass_mask.notes: Mask each glass pane perimeter along muntin edges. ~5 LF tape per pane. Conditional on French door type.

required_inputs.purpose: Count of door frame sets for material quantity calculation (frame primer + finish)
Count of door slab sides for material quantity calculation (slab primer + finish)
Total door openings for per-opening consumable calculations (protection, assessment)
Floor protection area for spray method
Wall masking perimeter for spray method
Total glass panes across all French doors for glass masking

compatibility_rules.description: Adhesion primer under any fine-finish system
compatibility_rules.notes: Water-based adhesion primer is compatible with all fine-finish topcoat chemistries. Scuff sand primer before finish coats.

compatibility_rules.description: Shellac stain blocker under any fine-finish system
compatibility_rules.notes: Shellac seals stains and is compatible with all topcoat chemistries. Universal undercoat.

compatibility_rules.description: Mildew primer under any fine-finish system
compatibility_rules.notes: Latex-based mildew primer is compatible with all fine-finish topcoat chemistries.

compatibility_rules.description: Modified urethane finish over previously painted surface
compatibility_rules.notes: Modified urethane finish coats adhere well to deglossed/primed existing coatings. Adhesion primer recommended when existing coating is oil-based or high-sheen.

risk_notes.risk: Interior doors historically received oil-based paint. Latex over un-primed oil-based coating will fail.
risk_notes.mitigation: Always perform coating ID test (solvent rub with mineral spirits) during assessment. If alkyd/oil identified, adhesion primer is mandatory. Never skip primer over oil-based existing paint.

risk_notes.risk: Overworking modified urethane products causes roping/brush marks on door faces -- highly visible defect on scrutinized surface.
risk_notes.mitigation: Apply, tip once, walk away per FFD 15.3.1. Do not go back and rework. Sand and recoat if defects remain.

risk_notes.risk: Doors may stick at hinge side or latch if paint is not fully cured before rehang. Especially acute with acrylic enamel (SYS_FF_STANDARD_ACRYLIC) which has softer film.
risk_notes.mitigation: Extended cure time before door rehang. Modified urethane and premium urethane have harder films and lower blocking risk. Do not close doors fully for 48-72 hours after final coat at minimum.

risk_notes.risk: Bathroom/kitchen door frame bottoms absorb moisture through end grain. Softened wood cannot hold paint. Painting over soft substrate causes premature failure.
risk_notes.mitigation: Assess frame bottom during assessment phase. If soft, apply CON_WOOD_HARDENER before filling and priming. If structural damage, flag for carpentry repair -- painting cannot fix structural compromise.

risk_notes.risk: Doors are HIGH RISK for lead paint -- trim/doors were the last interior surfaces to transition from oil to latex. Scraping/sanding on pre-1978 doors generates lead-containing dust.
risk_notes.mitigation: MOD_RRP_INT_CONTAINMENT module is conditional on PS_META.BOOL.HOME_PRE_1978. RRP-certified renovator required. Containment, HEPA vacuum, and wet methods per EPA RRP Rule.

risk_notes.risk: Excess material accumulates in rail-stile joints and panel recess corners during brush application. Results in visible drips and uneven sheen.
risk_notes.mitigation: Load brush lightly, work coating out of crevice onto flat surface. Tip from inside corner outward. Check for drips 5-10 minutes after application during flash time.

material_notes.selection_guidance: Material system selection follows Fine Finish Doctrine: QT3 = SYS_FF_STANDARD_ACRYLIC, QT4 = SYS_FF_MODIFIED_URETHANE, QT5 = SYS_FF_PREMIUM. Door frames and door slabs use the same finish system. RP primer selection is state-driven (adhesion, stain-block, or mildew) and independent of finish system selection.
material_notes.coverage_variability: Door coverage is EA-based (frame: ~30 SF equivalent per EA, slab: ~20 SF per EA_SIDE). Slab coverage varies significantly by door type: slab doors are 10% more efficient, panel doors 10% less, French doors 40% less, louvered doors 60% less than standard average.
material_notes.rp_vs_nc_differences: RP uses state-driven RP primers (SYS_PRIMER_ADHESION_INT, SYS_PRIMER_STAINBLOCK_INT, SYS_PRIMER_MILDEW_INT) instead of NC substrate-driven primers. RP primer coverage is higher than NC because previously painted surfaces absorb less. RP adds TSP wash, deglosser, assessment kit, wood hardener, and contour sanding sponges not needed in NC.
material_notes.open_time_by_chemistry: Standard acrylic enamel has moderate open time. Modified urethane/waterborne alkyd (Advance, Emerald Urethane) has SHORT open time (5-10 min) -- do not overwork per FFD 15.3.1.
material_notes.coat_count_summary: QT3-QT4: 2 finish coats standard. QT5 brush: 3 finish coats per FFD 15.10.3. QT5 spray: 2 finish coats. Prime coat (when applicable) is always 1 coat.

assumptions.value: Frame set = 30 SF equivalent, slab side = 20 SF equivalent
assumptions.source: Standard residential door dimensions (3'0" x 6'8" slab, standard frame profile)
assumptions.note: Industry standard EA-to-SF equivalents. Tall doors (H2) have ~15% more SF per EA.

assumptions.value: RP adhesion primer at 425 SF/gal vs NC bare-wood primer at 300-350 SF/gal
assumptions.source: Previously painted surfaces absorb less primer than bare wood
assumptions.note: No doctrine defines RP vs NC primer coverage differential. Derived from product PDS typical coverage range and field practice.
TSP is new to the consumable registry. Yield based on standard dilution ratio and wipe-down coverage per door opening.

assumptions.value: 10 frames per tube (selective replacement vs NC full caulk at 8-10 per tube)
assumptions.source: Materials_and_Consumables_Doctrine caulk section + RP selective replacement logic
assumptions.note: RP assesses and replaces only deteriorated caulk joints. Yield per tube is similar to NC because RP replacement sections are shorter but require more tooling per section.
